title: Kindred in Christ, for His Dear Sake
description: Kindred in Christ, for His Dear Sake in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book II, hymn 70, “A welcome to christian friends”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Kin-dred in Christ, for his dear sake, A hear-ty wel-come here re-ceive; May we to-ge-ther now par-take The joys which on-ly he can give!

lines: Kindred in Christ, for his dear sake,
A hearty welcome here receive;
May we together now partake
The joys which only he can give!
To you and us by grace 'tis giv'n,
To know the Savior's precious name;
And shortly we shall meet in heav'n,
Our hope, our way, our end, the same.
May he, by whose kind care we meet,
Send his good Spirit from above,
Make our communications sweet,
And cause our hearts to burn with love!
Forgotten be each worldly theme,
When christians see each other thus;
We only wish to speak of him,
Who lived, and died, and reigns for us.
We'll talk of all he did and said,
And suffered for us here below;
The path he marked for us to tread,
And what he's doing for us now.
Thus, as the moments pass away,
We'll love, and wonder, and adore;
And hasten on the glorious day,
When we shall meet to part no more.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
